newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast gasoline up with NYMEX, low stocks.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast gasoline up with NYMEX, low stocks.

text.p: Wholesale prices for U.S. West Coast gasoline rose Thursday on moderate gains in crude futures and fears of low inventory, traders said.

NYMEX crude oil for May delivery rose 30 cents a barrel, as the nearby futures price for heating oil turned hot amid falling temperatures in the U.S. Northeast, the world's largest market for the fuel.
May heating oil rose 1.75 cents a gallon to 54.86 cents.
Despite cargoes, West Coast gasoline stocks fell short of year-ago levels by 2.3 million barrels, according to weekly inventory reports published by the industry and government.
Cargoes included a 486,000 barrel gasoline delivery on the ship Varden, which reached Los Angeles April 3, a trader reported.
Mobil and Chevron refineries have since bought some of its barrels on the spot market, traders said.
Traders could not could give specifics on the four other cargoes.

The balance between supply and demand was reflected in California refinery margins, which rose to $7.50 a barrel in early April, their highest level since the second quarter last year, said Salomon analyst, Paul Ting.
Ting doubted refining margins would reach double-digits in 1997. Offers for CARB unleaded gasoline in Los Angeles rose 1.50 to 67 cents, while bids rose a half cent.

Distillates were flat to softer, hit by early losses in heating oil futures followed by quiet afternoon spot trade on the West Coast. Jet fuel bids fell two cents a gallon in L.A. to 62 cents, while low sulphur diesel in San Francisco remained flat at 61.50/62.50 cents.
